1.explanation:
1. lib/rules/key-spacing.js is the implementation of the “key-spacing” rule. It contains the logic that determines when to apply singleLine vs. multiLine alignment, and it’s mis-detecting inline JSX objects as multiLine (or even breaking single-line objects open) and then re-aligning their values. 

2. tests/lib/rules/key-spacing.js is where you would add or update rule tests to capture this regression (i.e. ensure that objects inside JSXExpressionContainers are left untouched unless they already span multiple lines). By updating the implementation in key-spacing.js and adding a new test case here, you can both fix the behavior and guard against future regressions.

2.explanation: The key-spacing rule implementation in lib/rules/key-spacing.js is what enforces and fixes spacing around the colon in object literals. It currently treats any multiline ObjectExpression the same, including those inside a JSXExpressionContainer (e.g. style={{…}}). That extra pair of JSX braces causes the rule’s offset calculations to be wrong, so it realigns everything incorrectly. To resolve this bug, the rule needs to detect object literals nested in JSX expressions and either skip alignment or adjust its column-offset logic accordingly.
2.bug_scenario: When using ESLint’s key-spacing rule with the multiLine “align: 'value'” option on a JSX style={{…}} object expression, running eslint --fix will realign all the nested object properties inside the JSX curly braces. Because the rule doesn’t account for the extra pair of braces around the object in JSX, it computes the wrong column offsets and produces the ugly, over-aligned formatting shown in the screenshots.
